title: CmdPal: Use fallback v2 results for Indexer search

proposed_comments.body:
### Explain the cursor-relative offset

**Severity:** `low` (documentation)

Please document why this passes zero. `IRowset::GetNextRows` remembers the cursor between calls; zero skips no rows from the current position. This is not a paging bug, but without the comment it is easy to mistake zero for the first page and add a cumulative offset that skips valid results.

```suggestion
        // The rowset keeps its cursor between calls; zero skips no rows from that position.
        return FetchItems(0, limit, queryCookie, out hasMore, out notice);
```

**Verification:** The [OLE DB cursor contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/desktop/ms709827%28v=vs.85%29) and the existing call path agree. The suggestion changes only a comment.
proposed_comments.title: Explain the cursor-relative offset

confidence.rationale: OLE DB documents the cursor-relative offset, and the same rowset is reused. The literal suggestion applies as a single comment addition.

proposed_comments.body:
### Skip the unused notice when starting a fallback query

**Severity:** `low`

The fallback session discards the notice returned by `Query`, but building it can still call into the Windows Search catalog before the session fetches any results. `FetchNextItems` builds the notice again after fetching, when the query may have retried with wildcard matching. Please make the fallback interface start the query without building a notice, keep the post-fetch notice, and preserve the query-time notice used by `IndexerPage`. A shared query-start method with an explicit implementation of the fallback interface would let both callers keep their existing behavior without doing the unused catalog read.

**Verification:** Run `NoticeCommandPreservesSearchQuery` to check the fallback still displays a post-fetch notice, and check that `IndexerPage` still consumes its initial notice.
proposed_comments.title: Skip the unused notice when starting a fallback query

confidence.rationale: The discarded return and potential catalog call are directly visible. This avoids unused work; no latency improvement is quantified.
